sentences.text: Brachyosteus was an extinct arthrodire placoderm, a class of armored fish known for their bony plates.
This animal belongs to the family Selenosteidae within the larger clade Aspinothoracidi.
The genus Brachyosteus was first described by Jaeckel in 1927.
The specific species Brachyosteus dietrichi was later named by Gross in 1932.
According to the Paleobi Database, the parent group of Brachyosteus is listed as Trematosteidae.
It lived during the Late Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
Fossils of this species have been found in Bad Wildungen, Germany.
